hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: US strikes three Iranian tankers after missiles fly at a carrier
brief.h: CENTCOM says it disabled the crude carriers M/T Downy off Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask and destroyed the unladen M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman, in answer to IRGC ballistic missiles fired at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer that both evaded without casualties.
brief.t: Read the admiral's sentence, not the strike. Brad Cooper did not say the tankers were shooting at anyone; he said that if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost, taking out three of yours. That is an exchange rate between military risk and commercial cargo, published on purpose, and it is a different war than the one being fought last month. The United States has spent thirty years arguing that attacking merchant shipping is what the other side does. It has now made sinking oil hulls its declared answer to being shot at, and priced it at three-for-two.
brief.context: The rail is older than the headline. A US maritime blockade of Iranian ports entered enforcement on 13 April 2026, restricting access without distinction as to flag, and the machinery behind it - right-of-visit boarding, directed communications, naval escort - has been running since. Until this week those tools were used to stop cargoes leaving. Reporting on the policy change says a tanker-for-tanker rule was approved at presidential level, converting the same apparatus from interdiction into retaliation. The deciding desk is CENTCOM with an OFAC designation list behind it, not the State Department: every hull named is a vessel already inside a sanctions file, which is what makes the target legally cheap. Base rate to hold: in the 1980s tanker war, roughly 450 commercial vessels were hit over five years without either belligerent's export volumes collapsing - attrition on hulls moves insurance faster than it moves barrels. What would change this read is a strike on a laden hull with no Iranian ownership link, which converts a targeted campaign into a general threat to trade.

angles.effect: gain a proportionate-looking answer to missiles fired at a carrier that costs no American lives and needs no new legal authority, because every hull was already sanctioned

angles.party: Iran's export revenue and the IRGC's proxy budget
angles.effect: pay directly - this is the first time the shadow fleet itself, rather than its cargo's destination, has been treated as a military target

angles.party: Shipowners, charterers and their war-risk underwriters
angles.effect: pay indirectly and immediately; a hull can now be destroyed for who owns it rather than what it does, and that is repriced across the whole Gulf book, not just the Iranian slice
pay in product - distillate is already at its highest since mid-2022, and every barrel of heavy sour taken off the water tightens the crack rather than the crude

dec.kill: An Iranian strike on a laden, non-Iranian-linked tanker inside the international lanes, or a second US round hitting a hull outside the OFAC list. Either would mean the campaign has stopped being targeted and the tanker-for-tanker frame has broken down.

consp.claim: That Tehran's real strategy is not military at all - that Iran intends to drive crude to $1,000 a barrel to wreck the American economy and sink Trump politically, and that the tanker exchange is Iran deliberately baiting strikes that raise the price it collects on every barrel it still sells.
consp.spread: An all-caps /pol/ thread running today alongside /pig/ Persia Israel General, now at its 2040th edition, whose own header sarcastically counts Day 187 of the four-day special military operation to regime change Iran and Day 15 of economic D-Day.
consp.read: The oil-weapon-as-election-sabotage frame, and the checkable kernel is real even though the number is not: Brent up 6.1 per cent on the week and US diesel at a 2022 high mean Iranian barrels removed from the water do raise the value of Iranian barrels still moving. What the frame cannot survive is arithmetic - Iran needs export volume to fund the state, and a price it cannot sell into is not leverage. Note also the board's own sarcasm about the day-counts: after six months the regulars are discounting their own happening posts, which is narrative fatigue and a signal in itself.

brief.head: Putin and Zelensky halt strikes as Trump envoys land in Moscow
brief.h: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight and Zelenskyy said Ukraine would hold off on Moscow until Monday, as Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived to be met by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev - while spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there was no talk of new ideas.
brief.t: The reciprocity is the news and the expiry date is the caveat. In four and a half years this war has produced plenty of unilateral pauses announced for Orthodox Christmas or a summit photograph; what it has not produced is both capitals agreeing to stop hitting each other's capital at the same time, for the same reason. That is a small thing that is structurally new. But read what it is scoped to: two cities, three days, and the duration of a visit. A ceasefire is a line on a map that both armies describe out loud. This is a security arrangement for a motorcade.
brief.context: The constraint to lead with is not Putin's mood but Washington's attention budget. The American push to end this war stalled through the summer for a reason the Kremlin can read as easily as we can - the United States has been at war with Iran since the spring, and a war on the export tape consumes the same principals, the same carrier groups and the same envoys. Witkoff and Kushner are themselves the tell: this is run out of a personal-envoy channel reporting to the President, not out of State, which means it can move fast and bind nothing. Peskov lowering expectations before the meeting even starts is the standard Kremlin move to keep the price of walking away at zero. The base rate is unkind - no pause in this war has survived its own expiry without a written text, and there is no text. Watch the Kyiv leg on Sunday: envoys who arrive with something specific are carrying an offer, envoys who arrive to explain are carrying a message.

angles.effect: gains a visible de-escalation in the same week it escalated in the Gulf - a peace story on one board while sinking tankers on the other
buys three days of not being struck in Moscow for three days of not striking Kyiv, at a moment when Ukrainian deep strikes have been reaching Sochi; the no-new-ideas line keeps the concession at zero
gains a night of sleep and a seat, and pays by parking its own long-range campaign - one of its few instruments of pressure - at American request
pay the whole cost of the framing: the pause covers one city, and the front line is not in it

dec.kill: An extension past 8 September, or a demarcation both delegations describe publicly, would mean this was a negotiation rather than a visit arrangement. A strike on Kyiv or Moscow before Monday kills it outright.

consp.claim: That the envoys' aircraft made an unexplained two-hour stop in Helsinki on the way to Moscow which the Finnish government has refused to comment on, and that the real meeting - the one with the actual terms - happened on the ground in Finland rather than in the Kremlin.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread built on a report in the Finnish paper Ilta-Sanomat about the aircraft's time on the ground, circulating alongside a separate thread arguing that the Kyiv government is the party that does not want the war to end.
consp.read: The secret-real-meeting frame, which attaches itself to every shuttle mission and has an unusually checkable kernel here: the stopover and the official silence are both reported by a mainstream Finnish outlet, and Helsinki has hosted exactly this kind of pre-meeting before. The inference that terms were agreed there is unsupported - crew rest and diplomatic clearance explain a two-hour turnaround at least as well - but the observation is real, and whether any Finnish official confirms a meeting is checkable within days.

brief.head: US oil bet on 17 Venezuelan fields faces a years-long wait
brief.h: Caracas has granted 100-year concessions over 17 fields holding some 65 billion barrels to Alejandro Betancourt's North American Blue Energy Partners, which currently pumps just over 200,000 barrels a day and says it will spend up to $100 billion to reach 1.5 million.
brief.t: Put the two numbers next to each other and the story writes itself: 65 billion barrels in the ground, 200,000 barrels a day out of the ground. The gap between them is not a rounding error, it is a decade of capital, and the announcement is engineered so that the first number is the one that gets repeated. This is the oldest move in the resource-headline playbook - quote the reserve, imply the flow. Proven reserves are a geological estimate. Production is a plumbing fact. Nothing about signing a concession moves a barrel.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: a sovereign taking equity in an extraction venture and calling it a trade deal. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital holds 35 per cent of NABEP and the State Department has the right to buy 20 per cent of output at the cost of production, with preferential access to the rest - that is not title to oil in the ground, it is offtake-at-cost plus a stake in an operator. The deciding desks are OSC and Energy rather than Treasury, which tells you this is being run as industrial policy, not as sanctions relief. The physical constraint is the part nobody announces: Venezuelan extra-heavy crude needs diluent, upgraders, power and export terminals that have been degraded for a decade, and brownfield restarts move in months while new upgrading capacity moves in years. ExxonMobil's Darren Woods told the President directly that Venezuela is, as it stands, uninvestable without durable legal frameworks, and that Exxon would send only a technical team. The base rate from concession to material output on extra-heavy greenfield is three to seven years. And the barrel that would actually cut American diesel prices is not this one: Merey is refinery feedstock, and the distillate shortage sits downstream in coking and hydroprocessing capacity, not upstream in crude.

angles.effect: books a headline about the biggest oil deal in history and lower pump prices this autumn, against a delivery date in the 2030s nobody will be scored on

gain a US government partner and a 100-year concession, and - per Reuters - the closure of a Miami money-laundering inquiry in which he was named an unindicted co-conspirator over PDVSA funds, with a separate Spanish investigation still live
carries contingent risk without an appropriation - a 35 per cent equity position in a Venezuelan operator is a sovereign exposure to expropriation, price collapse and the next government in Caracas

angles.party: Canadian heavy producers and Gulf refiners
angles.effect: sit on the other side of the same trade; if this heavy barrel ever arrives at scale, the Western Canadian Select discount is where it shows up first
pay in the durability question - a 100-year concession signed by an interim arrangement is paper until institutions and contract sanctity exist

dec.kill: A named arbitration seat, a governing law and a published sanctions authorisation in the 8 September signing session would make this an instrument rather than a term sheet. A major with a balance sheet - not a technical team - committing capex would kill the uninvestable read outright.

consp.claim: That the whole Venezuela sequence was a corporate-state seizure from the start - that the boat strikes, the pressure campaign and the Pentagon's 35 per cent stake are the modern Dutch East India Company, a state chartering a private firm to hold territory and book the revenue, with the quietly closed money-laundering investigation as the receipt.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread arguing explicitly that the Trump government is creating a corporate state and reaching for the VOC as the historical template, running beside the long-standing oil-seizure thread and amplified on X off the Reuters and CNN reporting.
consp.read: The the-real-reason-is-the-oil frame, with an unusually strong checkable kernel: the equity stake, the offtake-at-cost right and the paused Miami inquiry are all in mainstream reporting, and the chartered-company comparison is analytically closer than it is comfortable - a defence ministry taking equity in a foreign extraction venture is genuinely that structure. What the frame adds beyond the record is intent and sequencing, and there the boring explanation - improvise a deal around the only producer still pumping - still fits the facts.

brief.head: Israel says it has taken Lebanon's Ali al-Taher ridge from Hezbollah
brief.h: Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israeli forces had driven Hezbollah out of a tunnel network under the contested highland - 15km from the border, 600 metres above sea level, overlooking much of southern Lebanon and northern Israel - three months after a June ceasefire.
brief.t: Terrain is the one asset in this conflict that does not expire. Rockets are consumed, tunnels are rebuilt, commanders are replaced - but a ridge that sees 600 metres down into the Litani approaches is either held or it is not. Taking it converts a bombing campaign, which has to be renewed every week to mean anything, into an occupation, which means something merely by continuing. That is why the ridge is worth more to Israel than the tunnels under it.
brief.context: The mechanism is coercive leverage transferred to a third party. Analysts read the seizure as pressure aimed less at Hezbollah than at the Lebanese state: confront Hezbollah yourselves, or live with an Israeli position on the ridge indefinitely. That is the structure of the 1985 to 2000 security zone, and the base rate from that experience is the thing to keep - a buffer held to force a government's hand was held for fifteen years and produced Hezbollah rather than disarming it. Note also what the claim rests on: Katz asserted the tunnel clearance, Hezbollah has not commented, and no independent confirmation of the network has been published. The June ceasefire is now the second Israel-Lebanon arrangement in this war to be overtaken by ground movement rather than formally abandoned, which is a regime characteristic worth logging - agreements here are not broken, they are outlived.

angles.effect: gains permanent observation over the Litani approaches and a standing threat that costs little to maintain, plus a domestic win that does not require declaring the campaign over
pays the whole bill of the strategy - it is handed a choice between civil confrontation with Hezbollah and indefinite occupation, with no third option offered
loses terrain and the infrastructure under it, but gains back the recruiting argument the 1985 zone gave it - occupation is the condition under which it was created
pay in the daily casualties and displacement in the villages under the ridge, with no ceasefire mechanism now covering them

dec.kill: Independent imagery or a Hezbollah acknowledgement of the tunnel network would confirm Katz's account; an Israeli withdrawal from the ridge under the June framework, or a Lebanese Armed Forces deployment onto it, would mean this was a raid rather than a buffer.

consp.claim: That the war's stated objectives are a cover story that even its supporters have stopped believing - the running joke being a day-count of the two-day limited military offensive to end Hezbollah, now at day 1,061, and the four-day special military operation to regime change Iran, now at day 187.
consp.spread: The header of /pig/ Persia Israel General on /pol/, at its 2040th consecutive edition and repeated verbatim across every thread in the series.
consp.read: Less a conspiracy claim than an accusation of bad faith, and it maps onto the war-duration-as-coalition-tell frame: a campaign sold as days that runs years is simultaneously a planning failure and evidence about who actually holds the file. The kernel is checkable and correct on the arithmetic - the dates are real. What it misses is that indefinite duration can be the objective rather than the failure, which is exactly what taking a ridge rather than a target implies.

brief.head: China presses on with Himalayan mega-dam above India's water supply
brief.h: Beijing is proceeding with the 60GW Medog cascade on the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet - five dams, roughly three times the Three Gorges, due on line from 2033 - despite warnings that Chinese scientists themselves have raised about building it in one of the world's most active seismic belts.
brief.t: This is the least-covered chokepoint on the board and the only one that cannot be re-routed. Oil finds another hull and chips find another fab, but the Brahmaputra has one source and it is upstream of 130 million people in India and Bangladesh. Whoever holds the gates on that river holds a tap on roughly a third of India's freshwater and about 55 per cent of Bangladesh's irrigation - and unlike a strait there is no international lane, no underwriter, and no convoy that can be run around it.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: hydrological upstream leverage, which works without ever being used. A dam does not need to be closed to be coercive; it needs only to be capable of being closed, which converts every future Indian negotiation on every file into one conducted downstream. There is no comprehensive water treaty between China and India, only expire-and-renew hydrological data-sharing memoranda - precisely the kind of thin instrument that gets suspended as a signal. The deciding desk is the National Development and Reform Commission and the state construction group, not the foreign ministry, which is why Indian diplomatic representations have not moved the schedule. Two constraints cut against the alarm and belong in the same paragraph: the Brahmaputra picks up the large majority of its flow from monsoon rainfall below the Chinese border, so an upstream cascade controls far less of the annual volume than the headline implies, and run-of-river designs store much less than reservoir dams. The genuine risk Chinese seismologists have flagged is not weaponisation but failure - 60GW of cascade infrastructure sitting on the Himalayan collision front, where the 1950 Assam earthquake reached magnitude 8.6. The falsifier for the coercion read is simple: a binding flow-sharing treaty signed before first generation would mean the leverage was never the point.

angles.effect: gains up to 300 billion kWh a year of carbon-free generation for the western grid, a construction stimulus in Tibet, and a permanent lever over a neighbour it has an unresolved border with
pays in strategic dependence rather than in water volume today - and responds with its own downstream dam in Arunachal Pradesh, imposing on Bangladesh the same costs it objects to from China
pays twice and has no seat at either table; it is downstream of both projects and party to neither

angles.party: Communities in the Medog gorge and the Assam floodplain
angles.effect: carry the seismic and flood-surge risk that the generation figures do not price

dec.kill: A binding trilateral flow-sharing treaty, or Chinese publication of the seismic design case for independent review, would kill the coercion read. Suspension of the existing hydrological data-sharing memoranda during a border dispute would confirm it.

watch: Whether Iran answers the tanker strikes on hulls or on hulls plus a laden neutral. That is the line our Hormuz falsifier is drawn on, and it is not fired: the three ships struck today were Iranian-linked, the one furthest out was empty, and the ordnance was American. An Iranian attack on a laden, non-Iranian-linked tanker inside the international lanes fires it - eighteen days left to run.

Monday's open in crude and distillate. Brent finished near $95 and WTI near $90, up 6.1 and 8.3 per cent on the week, and the CENTCOM announcement landed with markets shut. The gap - or the absence of one - is the cleanest available read on whether professional money thinks tanker-for-tanker is a doctrine or a one-off.

Whether the 72-hour pause is extended past 8 September, and whether anyone tables a text. Peskov has already said there is no talk of new ideas, which sets the walk-away price at zero. A pause with an expiry is a meeting arrangement; a demarcation both delegations describe in public is a negotiation. The Kyiv leg on Sunday is where that becomes visible.

The Saxony-Anhalt SEAT count on Sunday night, not the vote share. A firewall only binds a party that needs a partner - an absolute majority makes it irrelevant, and a near-miss forces a CDU that has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke to build a majority out of roughly a third of the chamber.

Whether the 8 September Venezuelan session produces an instrument - a governing law, an arbitration seat, a named sanctions authorisation - or another briefing. And whether any major with a balance sheet, rather than a technical team, commits capex against the 17 fields.
lesson: Today's mechanism has a French name and a German test tomorrow: the cordon sanitaire, the agreement among mainstream parties never to govern with a particular party - in Germany they call it the Brandmauer, the firewall. It matters to see what kind of instrument it actually is, because almost everyone describes it wrongly: a cordon is not a ban and it removes nobody from a ballot, it is a COALITION rule, and coalition rules only bind a party that needs a partner. That is why a party at 33 per cent is contained by it and a party at 45 per cent is not, and why the seat arithmetic in Saxony-Anhalt matters more this week than any speech about democratic norms. The scholarship is genuinely split and you should be told so rather than sold a side: van Spanje and van der Brug found in 2007 that ostracism can push a radical party to moderate its programme in order to become coalitionable, while other work in the same literature finds it hardens the outsider identity the party runs on - Austria's Freedom Party entered government in 2000 and later shrank, Belgium's Vlaams Belang has been cordoned for thirty years and has not. What the theory does predict robustly is the second-order cost nobody campaigns on: every additional party a mainstream bloc excludes shrinks the arithmetic it has left, and Germany's Christian Democrats have now excluded two, so a firewall that holds on Sunday may buy an ungovernable state rather than a governed one. Watch for that branch rather than the dramatic one - it is the likelier outcome, and it is the one that decides whether the rule survives the election after this one.

quiz.q: Iranian state media says US missiles hit a tanker near Kharg Island. Why did the brief treat WHERE it happened as the load-bearing detail?
options: Because Kharg sits inside the Strait of Hormuz and closing the strait was the objective
Because Kharg is the loading anchorage rather than the transit lane - so the target shifts from whether Iran's oil can pass to whether Iran can sell at all
Because the island is uninhabited and therefore a safe target
Because it is closer to Iraq than to Iran
quiz.why: Kharg lies roughly 250 nautical miles up the Gulf from the strait. Attacks in the transit lane are about passage; an attack at the loading point is about export capacity itself - which is also why our own published Hormuz falsifier, written on the international lanes, did NOT fire today, and we said so rather than quietly rewording it.

quiz.q: Russia paused strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours and Ukraine paused its air attacks. Why did the brief call this a meeting arrangement rather than a ceasefire?
options: Because ceasefires have to be registered at the United Nations
Because Russia has never paused anything before, so it cannot be genuine
Because it has a stated purpose and an expiry, covers one city, and comes with no demarcation line, no monitoring and no guarantor - the three features that make ceasefires last
Because Ukraine did not actually agree to it
quiz.why: Fortna's finding is that ceasefires endure when they have monitoring, demarcation and third-party guarantees. A three-day pause over one city, tied to a visit, has none of the three - which is why the ledger moved three points rather than twenty.

quiz.q: Germany's mainstream parties refuse to govern with the AfD. Why does the brief argue that refusal could stop working on Sunday?
options: Because a firewall is a coalition rule, and coalition rules only bind a party that needs a partner - an absolute majority of seats makes it irrelevant
Because the constitutional court is about to strike the policy down
Because the CDU has announced it is dropping the policy
Because the AfD has moderated its programme to qualify
quiz.why: This is the whole mechanism. A cordon sanitaire is not a ban and removes nobody from a ballot; it denies partners. At a high enough seat share, with small parties missing the five per cent threshold, a party stops needing any - which is why the seat count matters more than the vote share.

quiz.q: The Pentagon holds 35 per cent of the Venezuelan venture and State can buy 20 per cent of output at cost. Which observable did the brief say would actually show a pre-built supply rail rather than spoils?
options: A larger equity stake
An on-the-record statement from the Office of Strategic Capital
A rise in Venezuelan production volumes
An awarded, funded dredging contract or a dedicated heavy-crude terminal tender
quiz.why: Equity is a claim on barrels; logistics is what moves them. Orinoco extra-heavy crude is near-solid at reservoir temperature and needs diluent, upgraders, power and channel depth - so capital works, not percentages, are the premeditation tell this board tracks as GEO-022.

quiz.q: CRITICAL THINKING. A claim circulating this weekend says the Kharg tanker strike proves a general war is days away. Which observable would most usefully test the CLAIM ITSELF?

Whether oil opens higher on Monday
Whether the account making the claim has been right before

Whether any independent party confirms the strike at all - CENTCOM, imagery, a war-risk insurer entry, a hull identification - and whether the 1984-88 tanker war, in which roughly 450 ships were attacked without either side's exports permanently stopping, actually predicts escalation to general war
quiz.why: Two moves in one. First sourcing: the only source right now is the party the story benefits, and the absence of independent confirmation is itself data. Second base rate: the closest historical analogue produced four years of attacks on shipping and no general war - so the claim has to explain what is different this time, not merely that it feels urgent.

sections.t: US diesel set an all-time record this week at $5.820 a gallon, and the crack spread — the refiner's fee for turning crude into something an engine can burn — printed an all-time $108 a barrel while Brent sat at an unremarkable $96. In the same week US missiles reportedly struck a tanker at Iran's Kharg Island anchorage, and Ukrainian drones held Russian refinery runs at 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since May 2002.

Crude — the thing everyone photographs and embargoes — is behaving; refined product is not. A $108 crack means the market will pay more to convert a barrel than the barrel is worth: a fact about cokers and hydrotreaters, not about oil. Name the mechanism — the conversion bottleneck. The binding constraint is never the abundant input but the narrow step in the middle, which cannot be built on the timescale of a war or an election.

sections.h: Deep history I — Rockefeller never wanted the oil
sections.t: John D. Rockefeller owned almost no wells. He owned the refineries of Cleveland, and what he did with them in 1871 is the founding text of chokepoint economics. Tom Scott of the Pennsylvania Railroad chartered the South Improvement Company, and Rockefeller's terms inside it were breathtaking: the Erie, New York Central and Pennsylvania would pay the SIC a rebate of $1.06 on every barrel it shipped — and a drawback of $1.06 on every barrel shipped by refiners outside the club. He was paid when his rivals did business. The charter was repealed that April before a single transaction cleared, and Ida Tarbell's exposé later finished the job — but the insight outlived the scandal: crude is worthless until someone converts and moves it, and whoever owns the narrow step prices the wide one.

sections.h: Deep history II — the war decided at the still
sections.t: The largest test of this proposition was the Allied air war, fought inside the alliance before it was fought over Germany. Arthur Harris of RAF Bomber Command believed in punishment: burn the cities, break the will. Carl Spaatz and Arthur Tedder pushed what Harris dismissed as panacea targets — oil. Germany had almost no crude. It had Bergius hydrogenation, synthetic fuel pressed from coal at Leuna, Pölitz and Brüx, plants too enormous to hide. The oil plan began in May 1944. Leuna alone absorbed 22 raids, 6,552 bomber sorties and 18,328 tons of bombs across a year, behind Europe's heaviest flak concentration. It worked anyway. German synthetic output fell from a peak of 316,000 tons a month to 107,000 in June 1944 and 17,000 by September. Aviation gasoline — the specific fraction, not oil in general — went from 175,000 tons in April to 5,000 in September: 97% gone in five months. From May 1944 Germany consumed more than it produced every month, and the stockpile was gone in six.

sections.h: Deep history II — the fuel, not the factories
sections.t: The detail that makes it unforgettable: over the same period Albert Speer drove German tank and aircraft PRODUCTION to its wartime peak. The Reich ended 1944 with more airframes than it could fly and more panzers than it could move — the factories were fine and the fuel was not. The US Strategic Bombing Survey — written by people with every reason to praise bombing in general — judged the oil and transport campaigns decisive and the city campaign not. Japan lost the same way: the July 1941 freeze is remembered as an oil embargo, but the fatal shortage was 100-octane aviation gasoline, a conversion capability Japan could not build.

sections.h: Deep history III — how the West stopped building stills
sections.t: Now the slow part. The last greenfield major refinery built in the United States was Marathon's Garyville, Louisiana: built 1973-76, online 1977, still running at 596,000 barrels a day. Fifty years, no new plants — and the base is now shrinking: about 132 operable refineries in January 2025 against more than 300 in 1981, with roughly 1.235m b/d of distillation capacity removed in seven recent closures and conversions, over 6.5% of the total. All of it while shale made America the largest crude producer in history at 13.86m b/d. The country built the well and stopped building the still. The capacity emigrated rather than vanished — Jamnagar runs 1.24m b/d, Dangote opened at 650,000 and plans 1.4m, China kept building — so the toll moved east and south, to jurisdictions happy to buy discounted sanctioned crude and sell the product back to the people imposing the sanctions.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: In all three cases the scarce thing is the transformation, and transformation capacity is inelastic over any politically relevant horizon: a new crude supplier takes a fortnight, a new hydrocracker takes five years and a billion dollars. Ukraine is now running the 1944 oil plan at a ten-thousandth of the cost, a drone flying 1,550km to Omsk doing what 6,552 B-17 sorties did to Leuna — Pape's denial thesis tested live. It breaks against me here: Germany had no crude and no neutral supplier, Russia has both, and a 24-year low in refining has not stopped Pokrovsk.

sections.h: The adjudication — Yergin and Blas vs Chris Miller
sections.t: THE ADJUDICATION — YERGIN AND BLAS versus CHRIS MILLER Yergin and Blas hold that energy chokepoints self-heal — inventories, bypass and rerouting absorb shocks forecast to be fatal — and they have been right about the barrel, Brent at $96 in a war that curtailed over 11m b/d. Chris Miller's Chip War argues the opposite for inputs that are not fungible: no reserve of fabs, no bypass for EUV, a decade to rebuild. The evidence splits them by step. Yergin and Blas won the crude argument; the crack is the market announcing the win does not survive one step downstream, because there is no strategic reserve of cokers — the US holds hundreds of millions of barrels of crude in the SPR and about a million barrels of distillate in the Northeast reserve, having stockpiled the input it cannot burn. Miller's case is still weaker in oil than in silicon: diesel is shippable in a way a fab's output is not, so refining heals in 12-24 months rather than 12-24 days.

OECD gasoline demand is in structural decline as EVs scale; diesel and jet demand are not, because trucks, ships, aircraft, mining and data-centre backup have no substitute. But a refinery makes every cut at once, so the economics that close Western refineries — falling gasoline — destroy the distillate capacity nobody meant to lose. A trap, not a cycle; confidence high. The bolder call, near 60%: by the mid-2030s the US is at once the world's largest crude exporter and a chronic net importer of middle distillates, and that buys a strategic PRODUCT reserve — legislated storage of diesel and jet, enacted after a winter shortage rather than before one. What keeps this honest is GEO-026: does the US diesel crack settle below $45 before 15 December 2026? It sits at 35%, so the house is 65% on regime rather than outage — and if the crack mean-reverts on the 2022 schedule, this is an elegant story about a spike, published as a miss.
